evidence.1_content: Read in full: what-is-an-llm, hooks-automation, transformers-attention, measuring-roi, first-automation, install-and-vault-setup, big-three-compared, codex-inside-claude-code, plus calling-an-llm-api and seo-with-ai in source. Teaching is accurate and current. Hooks: exit 2, stop_hook_active and permissionDecision are right. Transformers: prefill/decode, KV cache and prompt caching are explained correctly, with a worked example. ROI: worked numbers check out (13.3h to 5h, about $12k/yr, $1,960 cost). LLM API: the STOP/stop/end_turn finish reasons and Anthropic's required max_tokens are right. SEO: an accurate summary of Google's scaled-content policy. Weak spots: codex-inside-claude-code states anecdotal comparisons as fact ('Codex wins on cross-session consistency… more bounded work per token', 'roughly 90%… the last 10%') under a hype subtitle 'The 10% that completes it' and a '10x Better' video. calling-an-llm-api names only OpenAI Chat Completions, not the Responses API that new OpenAI projects now use. The Ollama example uses llama3.2. The longest lessons (Obsidian at 3.5k–4.4k words) are dense and repeat themselves.
evidence.2_relevance: No private or personal content was found: a grep for names, private apps, local paths and TODOs is clean, and every task has a generic running example (bookshop, tutoring business, yoga studio). Apply-it blocks speak to student, developer and professional in turn. The tilt is still visible. CLAUDE.md appears 197 times in content against 76 for AGENTS.md. The Obsidian pillar, which sits on the non-coder 'understand AI' route, is built around Claude Code and has a non-coder name a note 'CLAUDE' (install-and-vault-setup). The Get-Hired fast track includes Claude-specific lessons (CLAUDE.md & memory, Prompting Claude Code). Chat assistants, the pillar non-coders most need, has 3 lessons against 13 for Claude Code. 'Upgrade your AI setup' often feels shoehorned, for example a coding-agent CLAUDE.md rule in the no-code first-automation lesson (49 lessons carry an 'If you use a coding agent' sub-block).
evidence.3_learning_design: Strong core loop: recall-first recap, scenario self-checks with I got it / I missed it, commit-then-explain MCQs with plausible distractors (transformers-attention), 'Do these first' prerequisites, previous/next links and goal-aware /path. Gaps: 'Apply it' and 'Do this now' often ask for the same build twice (hooks-automation adds a lint hook in both; first-automation builds form→sheet→alert in both). Duplicate 'Success:' lines sit back to back (install-and-vault-setup apply-it). Time estimates count the full video even when the why-box says to watch a segment (install-and-vault-setup: header 'video 70', but only about 8.5 minutes is needed). Math & ML core is on none of the three routes. In the recap, 'Not yet' cards are not re-queued.
evidence.4_onboarding: Home makes clear within seconds what the site is (a free, vendor-neutral course), who it is for (students, developers, non-coding professionals) and where to start (Start Here plus three goal routes). The 'How every lesson works' strip and the About page are clear. On mobile at 375px the first screen is mostly the stats title block (Sections 2 / Pillars 12), and the headline only begins about halfway down.
evidence.5_navigation: Desktop has a sticky course sidebar with the current lesson marked, an on-page section jump bar (Watch … Notes), back to pillar, previous/next, and a mobile menu. Search is full-text, URL-synced (?q=&level=), has level filters and a helpful empty state. Nits: snippets show markdown leftovers (' - Time to first token (TTFT) : how long', 'product code .'). Ranking for a tool name is weak: 'cursor' returns 37 lessons led by Tokens & context, whose snippet never mentions Cursor. Start Here repeats the home route block word for word.
evidence.6_interactive: All tested and working. Mark complete persists across reload (aria-pressed=true). The note saved and reloaded. The recap flipped through 7 cards, scored 4/7 and showed 'Last time you recalled 4 of 7' on return. Self-check reveal plus self-grading works. MCQ marks the wrong answer struck through with ✗ and the right one with ✓, plus an explanation. The Get-Hired checklist persists (ai-learn:career:v1) and the readiness % updates. Dashboard XP, rank, badges, streak and per-pillar counts work. Export/import/erase code is sound: blob download, prefix-filtered import, confirm before erase. Opening a lesson no longer writes empty note keys. Nits: phases on /get-hired are a one-open-at-a-time accordion. The dashboard briefly shows '– / 106' and 'Continue → lesson 1' before it hydrates.
evidence.7_visual: The 'Computation Pad' look is distinctive and coherent: ruled title blocks, monospace numbers, restrained indigo and red pen. Prose is readable at 17px, and hierarchy is clear: numbered step boxes, H2/H3. Nits: the video placeholder is a flat black box on desktop before play (the thumbnail showed on mobile). The OG share image renders in a generic system sans instead of the site fonts, has an empty lower half and a hyphen break ('self-/check'). Emoji in recap cards and badges sit awkwardly beside the print aesthetic. Very long lessons are text walls with few visuals or diagrams (transformers-attention has no attention diagram).
evidence.8_mobile: No page overflows sideways at 320 or 375 across 17 pages: home, start-here, sections, pillar, 6 lessons, search, dashboard, get-hired, path, about, 404. Code blocks scroll inside their own box. The header collapses to Menu, and the lesson jump bar becomes 'Jump to a section'. The only small targets are inline text links. Nit: at 320px with the menu open, the 'Close' button sits flush to the right edge with no gutter (right edge 318.9px).
evidence.9_accessibility: Skip link, labelled navs (Main, Course contents, On this page, Lesson navigation), one H1 with H2/H3 in order, a global :focus-visible outline, a label on the search field, aria-pressed on filters and toggles, aria-expanded on reveals, native labelled checkboxes, MCQ options grouped with aria-labelledby, aria-live feedback, and a prefers-reduced-motion block. Contrast holds: muted #4e5566 on the sheet ≈6.2:1, print ≈8.3:1, red pen ≈4.65:1. Nits: self-check aria-controls points at an id that isn't in the DOM while collapsed. The lesson H1 contains the subtitle, so it reads as 'RAG fundamentalsGive the model your data'.
evidence.10_trust: Strong: every video names its channel and year and has a 'Why this one' that discloses vendor bias (Asana, Nathan Gotch). The About page says plainly that lessons were drafted with AI assistance and checked against sources, and explains what a review covers. There are no cookies or analytics, YouTube loads only on play (nocookie), and each lesson has a report-an-error link. Weaknesses: all 106 lessons show the same 'Reviewed 3 Oct 2026' (explained on About, but a blanket stamp undercuts the signal). A few unsourced or anecdotal claims are stated as fact (codex-inside-claude-code division of labor). Hype-titled videos remain primaries ('Make Claude Code 10x Better').
evidence.11_technical: All main routes return 200 in under 20ms. The 404 page is friendly and links to search and Start Here. Per-lesson canonical, og and twitter tags plus a 1200×630 OG image are present, html lang=en, the sitemap has 126 URLs, and robots is fine (localhost absolute URLs are expected pre-release). Nits: the console showed repeated 'Unrecognized feature: web-share' warnings and several 404 resource errors during the session (local Next assets all returned 200, so the 404s likely came from third-party or YouTube requests or from my 404 probes; worth confirming). The OG image is unbranded and typographically weak. Search snippets leak markdown.

fixes.issue: The Claude tilt reaches the non-coder routes: the Obsidian pillar is built around Claude Code and a note named CLAUDE, and CLAUDE.md outnumbers AGENTS.md 197:76.
fixes.fix: Call the vault rules file a neutral name (e.g. RULES.md or AGENTS.md) in the no-code path and add a one-line note to symlink or copy it to CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md for agents. Give the default examples outside the Claude Code pillar as AGENTS.md first, CLAUDE.md as an alternative.

fixes.issue: The non-coding professional route is thin: Chat assistants has 3 lessons while Claude Code has 13, and 'Upgrade your AI setup' often adds coding-agent advice to no-code lessons.
fixes.where: content/foundations/chat-assistants/, first-automation.mdx and the other 49 lessons with 'If you use a coding agent'
fixes.fix: Add 3–5 chat-assistant lessons (writing and editing with AI, data analysis on uploaded files, meetings/email/documents, images and voice, building a Custom GPT/Gem/Project). Drop the coding-agent sub-block from lessons on the no-code route unless it is genuinely specific.

fixes.issue: 'Apply it' and 'Do this now' often ask for the same build, so the learner does one task twice or skips one.
fixes.fix: Make 'Apply it' a short transfer exercise on the learner's own context (a decision, a plan or a 10-minute adaptation) and keep the single hands-on build in 'Do this now'. Audit every lesson for overlap.

fixes.issue: Header time counts the full video when the lesson says to watch a segment, and 'Success:' lines appear twice in a row.
fixes.where: install-and-vault-setup (video 70 vs 8.5 min needed), other Obsidian lessons, codex-inside-claude-code
fixes.fix: Add a watchMinutes field used by the header ('video 9 of 70') and deep-link the start time (?start=71). Remove the duplicate Success line when the prompt already contains one.

fixes.issue: Math & ML core is on no route, and 'Not yet' recap cards aren't revisited.
fixes.fix: Add an optional 'Then 8 · Math & ML core' to the build-software route. Re-queue 'Not yet' cards at the end of the recap.

fixes.issue: Anecdotal comparisons are stated as fact, and the framing is hype.
fixes.fix: Retitle the subtitle (e.g. 'A second lab as reviewer'). Remove '90% / last 10%'. Hedge or source the 'Codex wins / Claude Code wins' list. Consider a primary video without a '10x' title, or note its framing in the why-box.

fixes.issue: Some API and tool examples lag 2026 practice.
fixes.where: calling-an-llm-api (Chat Completions only), transformers-attention (ollama run llama3.2)
fixes.fix: Mention OpenAI's Responses API and its status/incomplete_details next to Chat Completions. Use a current small open model in Ollama examples.

fixes.issue: The longest lessons are walls of text with no diagrams.
fixes.fix: Trim repetition by about 20% and add one simple inline SVG per architecture-heavy lesson (e.g. a Q·K·V attention flow and the prefill/decode timeline).

fixes.issue: All 106 lessons share an identical 'Reviewed 3 Oct 2026' stamp, which reads as automatic.
fixes.fix: Show the review date plus a short per-lesson change note (e.g. 'Reviewed 3 Oct 2026: video replaced, hooks events updated'), or a 'last substantive change' date next to it, so the date carries information.

fixes.issue: Hype-titled vendor videos serve as primaries.
fixes.where: codex-inside-claude-code ('Make Claude Code 10x Better'), big-three-compared ('Worth Your Money?')
fixes.fix: Prefer neutral primaries where a comparable one exists, or keep the why-box disclosure and move the hype-titled video to backups.

fixes.issue: The video slot is a flat black box on desktop before play, and the OG image is unbranded.
fixes.where: YouTubeEmbed placeholder on desktop lesson pages; src/app/**/opengraph-image
fixes.fix: Always render the YouTube thumbnail (i.ytimg.com) behind the Play button. Load Archivo/Atkinson into the OG ImageResponse, fill the lower half (lesson subtitle or pillar), and prevent the 'self-/check' hyphen break.

fixes.issue: Emoji in recap cards and badges clash with the print aesthetic.
fixes.fix: Replace emoji with drawn line icons or numbered ticks in the pad style, or render them monochrome.

fixes.issue: Search snippets leak markdown, and tool-name queries rank poorly.
fixes.fix: Strip list markers and bold spacing artifacts when building search-index.json. Boost title, subtitle and tags matches, and show the snippet window around the matched term.

fixes.issue: The console shows repeated 'web-share' warnings and 404 resource errors during lesson browsing.
fixes.where: lesson pages (YouTubeEmbed iframe allow list or third-party requests)
fixes.fix: Remove 'web-share' from the iframe allow attribute (or keep it only where supported). Trace the 404s in the network panel and fix or silence them.

fixes.issue: On phones the first screen is mostly the stats block; the value proposition starts mid-screen.
fixes.fix: On small screens put the headline and Start Here above the stats title block, or collapse the stats into one line.

fixes.issue: The H1 accessible name runs the title and subtitle together, and aria-controls targets an unmounted id.
fixes.fix:
Move the subtitle out of the H1 (a

under it) or add a visually hidden separator. Render the answer region always (hidden) or drop aria-controls while collapsed.

verdict: A genuinely good free course: accurate, current teaching with worked examples, well-built recall and quiz mechanics, honest sourcing and privacy, and clean mobile and accessibility basics. It falls short of 9 on content, relevance and learning design because the Claude/coding-agent tilt still reaches the non-coder routes, the chat-assistant pillar is thin for professionals, and Apply-it and Do-now often duplicate each other. Smaller trust and polish issues remain: a blanket review stamp, a hype-framed Codex lesson, an unbranded OG image and leaky search snippets.
